The reduction to `t := toMeasurable volume s` works. `t` is measurable, so it is null-measurable. On `U`, `volume` comes from `measureSpaceOfInnerProductSpace`, and Mathlib has an `IsAddHaarMeasure` instance for it (Haar/OfBasis.lean). `U` is a finite-dimensional real normed space, so it is locally compact and sigma-compact, and a Haar measure on it is sigma-finite and hence s-finite. `Measure.restrict_toMeasurable_of_sfinite` exists in Typeclasses/SFinite.lean with only `[SFinite μ]` as hypothesis, and it gives `volume.restrict t = volume.restrict s`. `IntegrableOn F s` is by definition `Integrable F (volume.restrict s)`, so `hint` carries over to `t`. The theorem as stated, or `ae_summable_fiber` with `g := 1`, then makes almost every fiber `t ∩ f ⁻¹' {y}` finite. From `subset_toMeasurable` and `Set.Finite.subset` we get the same for `s ∩ f ⁻¹' {y}`. The argument has no gap, and the empty case is trivial.
